title: One-line collections
description:
Write each function body as a **single** `return` with a comprehension:

```python
def squares_of_evens(numbers): ...      # [4, 16] for [1, 2, 3, 4]
def word_lengths(words): ...            # {"fig": 3, "apple": 5}
def initials(names): ...                # sorted list of the distinct first letters, upper-case (skip empty names)
def transpose(matrix): ...              # rows become columns: [[1, 2], [3, 4]] -> [[1, 3], [2, 4]]
def flatten(lists): ...                 # [[1, 2], [], [3]] -> [1, 2, 3]
```

All rows of a matrix have the same length; an empty matrix transposes to an empty list.
hints: For `transpose`, the outer comprehension walks the column numbers, and the inner one picks that column from every row.
`flatten` is a comprehension with two `for` clauses, written in the same order as the nested loops would be.
